correctness.rationale: For A={0,e_1,...,e_7}, W_A(v)=8-2 wt(v); zero differences have weight four. The pairwise complements of seven differences form a Fano 2-(7,3,1) system, forcing the translated frequency set to be a three-dimensional simplex-code subspace. Counting distinct column arrangements modulo GL(3,2) gives 30 subspaces and 16 cosets each. Replacing the final vertex gives W_B-W_A=(-1)^{v_7}((-1)^{v·u}-1), so common spectra require u in the dual Hamming code. Its weight enumerator 1+7z^3+7z^4+z^7 plus S_7 incidence gives 30,6,0 qualifying subspaces. Distinct projected frequencies lift independently in d>7. Exact integer checks reconstructed every one of the 480 projected spectra and tested 64 mutations, 860160 distinct pair tests, and the 128-vector code incidences. Full proof, not finite experiments, justifies all dimensions and edge weights.

value.rationale: This complete classification answers a natural robustness question for simultaneous exponential measurement bases under a one-vertex perturbation of an eight-element affine-independent spectral set. Both supports always individually have spectra, yet a single changed vertex can destroy all common bases or preserve exactly 1/5, with a sharp Hamming-weight criterion. The Fano/Hamming mechanism is structural rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; the ambient lifting formula extends the theorem to all d>=7 and delineates a motivated quantitative boundary. The scope does not assert a general theorem for arbitrary support pairs.
